verdict: approve

Use `reject` when it does not do what the ticket asks, changes more than the ticket asks, or the evidence cannot show that it does. <ticket id="T-0011" kind="test" seat="harness-core-llm-pi-ai-steward">
title: Pin that one pi-ai stream() call makes exactly one provider request on a retryable failure
task: Problem: the adapter passes `maxRetries: 0` to the pi-ai SDK (packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/adapter.ts:96-97: 'The agent recovery layer owns visible attempts; one adapter call is one SDK attempt') and the README promises at packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md:118 that one `stream()` call makes one provider request, so that `dsh-llm-retry` and the session log own every visible attempt. Nothing pins it on a failure the SDK would retry: packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/adapter.spec.ts asserts a single request only where no retry could happen (an unsupported reasoning effort refused before sending, :560; a consumer abort, :987). A pi-ai upgrade that re-enabled retries, or a lost `maxRetries: 0`, would multiply requests and hide attempts from `llm/retry` without failing a test.

Required: add packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts using the existing `mockServer` helper (packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/mock-server.ts already scripts a non-200 `status` with headers) with a scripted response the SDK treats as retryable: one test with a 500 and one with a 429 carrying a `retry-after` header. Drive the real adapter through `ctx.llm.stream()` as adapter.spec.ts does and assert that the stream finishes with `kind: 'error'` carrying the mapped code (`SERVER`, `RATE_LIMIT`) and that `server.requests` has length 1 after the finish settles.

Constraints: do not mock pi-ai; extend tests/mock-server.ts only if a status-only script cannot express the case; no source change.
scope: packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/
generated: docs/subsystems/, docs/cordis-api/, docs/graph-atlas.*, docs/capability-seams.*, docs/event-producer-consumer.*, docs/agent-lifecycle.*, docs/tool-execution-pipeline.*, docs/tool-catalog.*, docs/config-catalog.*, docs/persistence-catalog.*, docs/module-graph.*, apps/cli/composition.*, examples/headless-agent/composition.*, examples/acp-agent/composition.*, packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts, packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/api-catalog.ts, packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/slot-catalog.ts, packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts, packages/core/scope/src/scoped-events.generated.ts
acceptance:
- spec: test -f packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts && pnpm exec vitest run packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts
- coverage: pnpm exec vitest run packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/ --coverage --coverage.include='packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/**/*.ts'
- typecheck: pnpm run typecheck
</ticket>

<diff>
diff --git a/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts b/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3c1345a5ed
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+/**
+ * One `ctx.llm.stream()` call makes one provider request, even when the
+ * failure is one the pi-ai SDK would retry. `dsh-llm-retry` and the session
+ * log own every visible attempt; an SDK-level retry would hide attempts from
+ * them.
+ */
+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
+import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
+import LlmRuntime from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
+import * as LlmPiAi from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai'
+import { assemble } from './assemble.ts'
+import { closeMockServers, mockServer, textEvents } from './mock-server.ts'
+
+afterEach(async () => {
+  vi.unstubAllEnvs()
+  await closeMockServers()
+})
+
+async function harness(baseURL: string): Promise<Context> {
+  vi.stubEnv('PI_TEST_KEY', 'test-key')
+  const ctx = new Context()
+  await ctx.plugin(LlmRuntime)
+  await ctx.plugin(LlmPiAi, {
+    providers: { deepseek: { apiKeyEnv: 'PI_TEST_KEY', baseURL } },
+  })
+  return ctx
+}
+
+describe('PiAiAdapter single provider attempt', () => {
+  it.each([
+    [500, 'SERVER', {}],
+    [429, 'RATE_LIMIT', { 'retry-after': '1' }],
+  ] as const)('makes one request when the provider answers %s', async (status, code, headers) => {
+    // Later scripted responses succeed, so an SDK retry would change both the
+    // request count and the finish.
+    const server = await mockServer([
+      { status, headers, body: JSON.stringify({ error: { message: 'retryable provider failure' } }) },
+      { events: textEvents },
+      { events: textEvents },
+    ])
+    const ctx = await harness(server.url)
+
+    const result = await assemble(ctx, { model: 'deepseek-v4-flash', messages: [] })
+
+    expect(result.finish).toMatchObject({ kind: 'error', failure: { code } })
+    expect(server.requests).toHaveLength(1)
+  })
+})
</diff>

verdict: approve

- **Scope:** The diff adds only `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/single-attempt.spec.ts`. There is no source change, no edit to `mock-server.ts`, and no mocking of pi-ai. The engine-scope check passed.
- **Cases:** It has the two cases the ticket names, via `it.each`. A 500 must map to `SERVER`. A 429 with a `retry-after` header must map to `RATE_LIMIT`. Both use `mockServer`'s existing status-and-headers script, so no helper extension was needed.
- **Real adapter:** The test builds a `Context`, loads `LlmRuntime` and `LlmPiAi` with a `baseURL` pointing at the mock server, and drives the stream through the `assemble` helper. It does not mock the adapter or the SDK.
- **Assertions:** The test checks `finish` matches `{ kind: 'error', failure: { code } }` and that `server.requests` has length 1. `assemble` waits for the stream to finish, so the request count is read after the finish has settled.
- **Sensitivity:** The mock server has two successful `textEvents` responses queued behind the failure. If an SDK retry came back, the request count would exceed 1 and the finish would no longer be an error, so a lost `maxRetries: 0` would fail the test. I did not run it with retries re-enabled, so that follows from the script rather than from an observed failure.
- **Checks:** The spec ran 2 of 2 passing. The full package run passed 215 tests at 100% coverage. Typecheck, lint, whitespace, documentation and committed checks all passed.
